5.1.crux: Coal formed from forests buried millions of years ago; heating it in factories gives coke, coal tar and coal gas.

cards.title: How coal formed

steps.text: About 300 million years ago, dense forests grew in low, wet lands
Floods buried the forests under soil
More and more soil piled up: high pressure and high temperature deep down
Over millions of years the dead plants slowly became coal

say: This slow change of dead plants into coal is called carbonisation.
Because coal is made from the remains of living things, it is a fossil fuel.
cards.remember: Coal = ancient forests, pressed and heated for millions of years.

cards.title: What we get from coal

items.name: Coke
items.eg: Almost pure carbon: used to make steel and extract metals

items.name: Coal tar
items.eg: Thick black liquid: dyes, drugs, paints, plastics, naphthalene balls

say: Coal tar is a mixture of about 200 substances.
Naphthalene balls that keep moths away are made from coal tar.

cards.title: Coal as a fuel

items.sub: Railway engines once ran on coal

say: Coal is hard and black, like stone.
Today roads are surfaced with bitumen, a petroleum product, instead of coal tar.

crux_points: Coal formed from buried forests over millions of years (carbonisation).
Processing coal gives coke, coal tar and coal gas.

quiz.q: The slow change of dead plants into coal is called…
quiz.why: Carbonisation turns buried plant remains into coal over millions of years.
Naphthalene is one of the many products obtained from coal tar.

5.2.crux: Petroleum formed from tiny sea creatures buried under the sea bed; a refinery separates it into useful parts like LPG, petrol, kerosene and diesel.

cards.title: How petroleum formed

steps.text: Tiny plants and animals lived in the sea
When they died, they sank and were covered with sand and clay
No air, high temperature and pressure for millions of years
They changed into petroleum and natural gas

say: Petroleum is a fossil fuel, just like coal.

cards.title: Under the ground
say: Petroleum is lighter than water and doesn't mix with it, so it sits above the water, with gas on top.
We drill wells to bring it up.

cards.title: Separating petroleum
say: Separating petroleum into its parts is called refining. It is done in a refinery.
Each part (fraction) is collected at a different height of the tall column.
cards.remember: Refining: one crude oil → many useful fractions.

cards.title: Black gold

items.sub: Hydrogen from natural gas makes urea

say: Useful substances made from petroleum and natural gas are called petrochemicals.
In India, oil was found in Assam in 1867. Today it also comes from Gujarat, Mumbai High and the Godavari and Krishna river basins.

crux_points: Petroleum formed from sea organisms buried for millions of years.
In the ground, gas lies above oil, and oil lies above water.
A refinery separates petroleum into LPG, petrol, kerosene, diesel, lubricating oil, wax and bitumen.

quiz.q: Which fraction is marked '?' at the top of the column?
quiz.why: The lightest fraction, petroleum gas, collects at the top.

quiz.q: Which petroleum product is used to surface roads?
quiz.why: Bitumen is the heavy, thick fraction used on roads and in paints.

5.3.crux: Natural gas is a clean fossil fuel that is easy to send through pipes; stored under high pressure it is called CNG.

cards.title: What is CNG?
say: CNG means Compressed Natural Gas.
Squeezing the gas into a small space makes it easy to store and carry in vehicles.

cards.title: Why it is a good fuel

items.sub: Buses and autos run on CNG
Piped to homes and power plants

say: Natural gas burns cleanly, which is why many cities use CNG buses.
cards.remember: CNG is called a cleaner fuel.

cards.title: Where it is found in India
say: Natural gas is often found along with petroleum.

crux_points: Natural gas is a fossil fuel found with petroleum.
CNG is natural gas stored at high pressure.
It is a cleaner fuel for vehicles, cooking and electricity.

quiz.why: CNG is natural gas compressed under high pressure.

quiz.q: Why do cities prefer CNG buses?
quiz.why: CNG burns cleanly and pollutes much less than petrol or diesel.

5.4.crux: Some resources, like sunlight and air, never run out; others, like coal and petroleum, are limited, so we must use them carefully.

cards.title: Two kinds of natural resources

cols.head: Inexhaustible
cells: Won't run out by human use

cols.head: Exhaustible
cells: Forests, minerals, coal, petroleum, natural gas

say: Fossil fuels took millions of years to form.
Once used up, they can't be made again in our lifetime.

cards.title: Save fuel on the road

items.text: Drive at a steady, moderate speed
Switch off the engine at red lights

say: These tips come from India's Petroleum Conservation Research Association (PCRA).
cards.remember: Use fuel only when needed: it's limited.

cards.title: Other ways to help

items.text: Switch off unused lights and fans

say: Saving electricity also saves coal burnt in power plants.

crux_points: Inexhaustible resources (sunlight, air) won't run out.
Exhaustible resources (coal, petroleum, natural gas, forests) are limited.
We must save fuel by driving sensibly and using less energy.

quiz.why: Sunlight will not run out because of human use.

options: Switching off the engine at a red light
quiz.why: An engine left running at a red light burns fuel for nothing.
